claim: The new proof of `Finset.mem_map_equiv` is two consecutive calls, `simp only [mem_map, Equiv.coe_toEmbedding]` and then `grind`, where a single `simp` call proves the statement. The PR's own profile shows this declaration getting slower (<10 ms before, 25 ms after), so the golf costs time, and a `simp only` + `grind` pair is fragile when the `simp only` output changes.
requested_change: Replace the two-line proof with the single call `simp [Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply]`, i.e. `theorem mem_map_equiv {f : α ≃ β} {b : β} : b ∈ s.map f.toEmbedding ↔ f.symm b ∈ s := by simp [Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply]`. If that is not at least as fast as the original proof, revert this declaration.
evidence: lean_verify_edit on Mathlib/Data/Finset/Image.lean, replacing Finset.mem_map_equiv with the body `simp [Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply]`: outcome `compiled`, no warnings. A single `grind [Equiv.coe_toEmbedding]` fails: grind keeps `⇑f.toEmbedding w = b` and never instantiates `Equiv.symm_apply_apply`. The PR description reports `Finset.mem_map_equiv`: <10 ms before, 25 ms after. A maintainers-only zulip_search finds a Dec 2025 #mathlib4 thread, '`simp only` + `grind` failure' (Kim Morrison, Jireh Loreaux), on `simp only` output changes breaking a following `grind`.

claim: `Finset.mem_map_equiv` is an `iff` characterisation of membership, but it is tagged only `@[simp 1100]`, not `@[grind =]`, even though its sibling `Finset.mem_map` directly above is `@[simp, grind =]`. `grind` cannot derive it from `mem_map`: this PR itself needs a `simp only` before `grind`, and `grind [Equiv.coe_toEmbedding]` alone fails.
requested_change: Tag the lemma `@[simp 1100, grind =]` so that `grind` can rewrite `b ∈ s.map f.toEmbedding` to `f.symm b ∈ s`.
evidence: file_read of target/Mathlib/Data/Finset/Image.lean lines 68-76: `mem_map` is `@[simp, grind =]` and `mem_map_equiv` is `@[simp 1100]` only. lean_verify_edit with `@[simp 1100, grind =]` plus the `simp [Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply]` proof: outcome `compiled`, no warnings. lean_verify_edit with the body `grind [Equiv.coe_toEmbedding]`: `grind` failed, with the E-matching diagnostics showing it stuck at `f.toEmbedding w = b`, `f.symm b ∉ s`.

claim: The new ending of `pi_map_piCongrLeft` takes two calls, `simp only [pi_pi, this]` and `exact Fintype.prod_equiv _ _ _ (congrFun rfl)`. The first rewrites with a local equation through `simp only`. The second leaves the equivalence `e` implicit and passes `congrFun rfl` for the pointwise hypothesis, which is just an obscured `fun _ ↦ rfl`. `Fintype.prod_equiv`'s own docstring points to `Equiv.prod_comp` as the version without that hypothesis, which is exactly the case here.
requested_change: Replace the last two lines with the single rewrite `rw [this, pi_pi, e.prod_comp fun i ↦ μ i (s i)]`. The minimal alternative is `rw [this, pi_pi]` then `exact e.prod_comp fun i ↦ μ i (s i)`.

claim: The new proof takes three steps: a `have` rewriting `ρ` to `ρ.fst ⊗ₘ ρ.condKernel`, then `simp only [this]` to rewrite the goal with that local equation, then `exact (compProd_apply_prod hs ht).symm`. A single `rw` performs all three. `simp only [this]` is also a nonstandard way to rewrite with a hypothesis.
requested_change: Replace the whole proof body with `rw [← compProd_apply_prod hs ht, ρ.disintegrate]`. Alternatively, to match the siblings `lintegral_condKernel` and `setLIntegral_condKernel` in the same section, use `conv_rhs => rw [← ρ.disintegrate ρ.condKernel]` followed by `rw [compProd_apply_prod hs ht]`.
